newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NYMEX to soon sign oil futures deal with Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX to soon sign oil futures deal with Hong Kong.

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) plans to sign an agreement with the Hong Kong Futures Exchange that would allow its crude oil futures to be traded there by the first quarter of 1997, NYMEX President Patrick Thompson said on Monday.
Thompson said the signing would take place next week, although he did not specify a date. It was expected trading would begin early next year.
NYMEX crude futures contracts are traded in New York on an open outcry basis. Outside New York pit trading hours, the futures can be traded on a screen-based system called Access.
Hong Kong would be the second Access centre in Asia after NYMEX set up an Access link with the Sydney Futures Exchange in September 1995.

Thompson told a news conference during the Asia-Pacific Petroleum Conference in Singapore that he hoped to resume talks with the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) about setting up an Access trading link in Singapore.
The talks have been held sporadically over the last 2-1/2 years, and Thompson said a link would complement the North Sea Brent futures contracts already traded on SIMEX.
NYMEX board member Albert Helmig said that most trading of NYMEX crude and Brent crude futures takes place when markets in New York and London are open, which supported a similar tie-up in Singapore.
The officials said the moves were part of a long-term NYMEX strategy to increase trading of its products in Asia.
NYMEX was considering Asia-specific products and was also exploring the potential for an Access link in China sometime in the future, they said.
